2608.20966.title: Structured but Fragile: On the Limits of LLMs in Cybersecurity Decision-Making
2608.20966.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in cybersecurity workflows, yet it remains unclear whether they can perform structured security reasoning or merely rely on superficial cues and prior knowledge. We study this question in the context of defence selection over attack graphs derived from real-world threat scenarios, including ransomware, supply-chain compromise, cloud abuse, Kubernetes attacks, POS malware, and ICS/OT intrusion. Given a budget constraint, LLMs must select security controls to minimise attacker success. We compare their strategies against each other and against a game-theoretic optimization baseline used as a normative reference for structured reasoning. Our results show that LLMs exhibit conditional competence. When explicit attack-graph structure is provided, they often produce coherent strategies close to the optimization baseline. However, their capabilities are fragile. LLM behaviour becomes increasingly fragile with graph complexity and is highly sensitive to framing. Small prompt changes can substantially alter rankings, and merely relabeling a poor strategy as ``optimal'' dramatically improves its evaluation. We further observe a non-monotonic relationship between formal risk and LLM judgement: strategies closest to the optimum are not necessarily ranked highest by LLM evaluators. To further probe reasoning ability, we ask LLMs to generate solvers for the same optimization problem. While the generated implementations recover the correct high-level formulation, they scale poorly compared to a purpose-built solver. Overall, our findings show that LLMs can approximate structured cybersecurity reasoning under controlled representations, but do not apply it robustly. This has important implications for the design and evaluation of AI-assisted security decision-support systems.
2608.20966.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在網絡安全工作流程中的使用日益增多，但仍不清楚它們是否能進行結構化的安全推理，或僅僅依賴表面線索和先前知識。<lb/>我們在防禦選擇的背景下研究這個問題，涉及從現實世界威脅場景中衍生的攻擊圖，包括勒索病毒、供應鏈妥協、雲濫用、Kubernetes 攻擊、POS 惡意軟件和 ICS/OT 入侵。<lb/>在預算限制下，LLMs 必須選擇安全控制措施以最小化攻擊者的成功率。<lb/>我們將它們的策略彼此進行比較，並與用作結構化推理的規範參考的博弈論優化基線進行比較。<lb/>我們的結果顯示，LLMs 表現出條件能力。<lb/>當提供明確的攻擊圖結構時，它們通常能生成接近優化基線的一致策略。<lb/>然而，它們的能力是脆弱的。<lb/>隨著圖的複雜性增加，LLM 的行為變得越來越脆弱，並且對框架高度敏感。<lb/>小的提示變更可以顯著改變排名，僅僅將一個不佳的策略重新標記為“最佳”會大幅改善其評估。<lb/>我們進一步觀察到正式風險與 LLM 判斷之間存在非單調關係：最接近最優解的策略不一定會被 LLM 評估者評為最高。<lb/>為了進一步探查推理能力，我們要求 LLM 生成相同優化問題的求解器。<lb/>雖然生成的實現恢復了正確的高層次表述，但與專門構建的求解器相比，其擴展性較差。<lb/>總體而言，我們的研究結果表明，LLMs 可以在受控表示下近似結構化的網絡安全推理，但並不穩健地應用它。<lb/>這對 AI 輔助的安全決策支持系統的設計和評估具有重要意義。
